name: Isidore de Lara
bio: Composer (1858-1935), born Isidore Cohen, whose operas were produced at Monte Carlo under the patronage of the Princess of Monaco. Wilde inscribed a copy of his Poems to him in June 1887: 'To my friend Isidore de Lara, the poet of the musicians, in sincere admiration and affection.'
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06, closing a nineteen-person backlog. NO CONNECTION LINE: the whole record is one inscription, and an inscription is not a relationship. IT IS KEPT BECAUSE OF WHAT IT SAYS - 'in sincere admiration and affection' is warmer than most of what Wilde wrote in books he gave away, and this map's rule is that warmth gets quoted whether or not it amounts to anything. BOTH INDEXES CHECKED BEFORE DECIDING: he has NO entry in the Index of Recipients - no letter to him survives - and a single General Index entry, 'De Lara, Isidore, 1136n'. So one footnote really is all there is, which is now a conclusion rather than an assumption. NOT CONSULTED: Osbert Sitwell's pen portrait of him in Noble Essences (1950), which the editors name.

context_engagements.note: One inscription, recorded without a connection line.

sources.quote: To my friend Isidore de Lara, the poet of the musicians, in sincere admiration and affection, Oscar Wilde, June '87.
sources.context: Wilde's inscription in a copy of his Poems (fifth edition, 1882), recorded by the editors in a note on de Lara's opera, produced at Monte Carlo under the patronage of Princess Alice of Monaco. NOT A LETTER: no correspondence between them survives and he has no entry in the Index of Recipients. The editors point to Osbert Sitwell's Noble Essences (1950) for a portrait.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The whole of the record: one inscription, in Wilde's hand, calling him a friend.
